subject: Private Offer: splitting term & pricing across business units — approval owners
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Tucker <alan.tucker@acme-corp.com>, procure_ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-09-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private Offer question — splitting term/pricing across divisions

Marissa,

Thanks for the call today. A quick follow up from procurement: Acme is trying to buy a company-wide license but needs two different contract term lengths and effective unit pricing for two divisions (CloudOps and Research). CloudOps wants a 24-month commitment at higher seat volume, Research wants a 12-month pilot at lower volume.

Can Redwood do a single AWS Private Offer with split pricing and different activation/approval owners per division? We also need to know who signs/approves on the Redwood side so our legal/procurement teams can map internal signoff flows.

Appreciate a simple breakdown (pricing delta, who needs to sign, how activation works in Marketplace after PO acceptance).

Lydia
Procurement Manager | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-03T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer question — splitting term/pricing across divisions

Lydia — thanks for the note and great questions. Short answer: yes, but there are tradeoffs to map out. See bullets below and attached "PO_Term_Options.pdf" for a compact matrix.

High-level options (pros/cons):
- Single private offer with multiple line items (recommended): one PO in AWS Marketplace that contains two line items, each with its own term length and price. Activation is per-line-item; Acme will see two entitlements once we activate the offer.
  - Pro: Single purchase/order flow for your procurement.
  - Con: Your internal buyer approval may need to include both division approvers up front (Finance/Procurement + BU managers).

- Two separate private offers (one per division): cleaner signoff mapping but requires two PO flows and separate activation steps.

Key questions for our side (so we can advise who signs):
1) Which Acme user/email will be the canonical buyer identity in AWS Marketplace (this is who we activate the offer to)?
2) Is Acme expecting a consolidated invoice or separate invoices per line item/division?

Who signs on Redwood side:
- Commercial approval and signature: Ben Carter (Director, Marketplace Sales Ops) — has delegated signatory for private offers up to standard discounts.
- Legal review/exception: Jonas Weber (Marketplace Counsel) — involved only for non-standard term language or custom SOWs.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm buyer identity and invoicing preference.
2) We share a pricing matrix (attached) and mark which approach you prefer.
3) If you want the single-offer route, Ben will prepare the private offer; Jonas will triage legal if SOW/custom language is requested.

I looped Ben and Jonas for operations and legal escalation. Happy to hop on a quick 20-minute sync if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachment: PO_Term_Options.pdf (1 page — matrix of line-item pricing by term/volume)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acme-corp.com>, Alan Tucker <alan.tucker@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T08:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer question — splitting term/pricing across divisions

Marissa / team — ack'd. Quick operational notes from Sales Ops:
- AWS allows multiple line items in one Private Offer; each line item can have its own term length and price. Activation is tied to the Marketplace buyer identity (the AWS Marketplace account/email you tell us).
- If Acme wants consolidated invoicing, we can set invoice routing to your billing contact — that'll push through Redwood's billing system after AWS activation (back-to-back invoice). Need the billing email.
- Approval owners: for private offers we typically need the AC's verbal signoff + procurement PO acceptance. Legal signature only if you require changes to our standard T&Cs/SOW.

Operational checklist (what I need from Acme):
1) Buyer Marketplace email/account to assign the offer to.
2) Billing contact for invoicing.
3) Confirmation on whether Research's pilot should be auto-renew or expire at 12 months.

If they want us to create a single private offer with two line items I can draft the private-offer payload and the DocuSign packet for commercial sign-off. If legal redlines arrive, Jonas — can you confirm your availability to review within 48 hours?

Ben Carter
Director, Marketplace Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer question — splitting term/pricing across divisions

Ben, Marissa — available to review. A couple of legal flags to call out:
- If Research's 12-month pilot requires trial licensing language (data retention/usage reporting), we should include a short SOW addendum rather than rework the Marketplace listing. That keeps the private offer payload standard and lets us attach the SOW off-band (SOW-summary.xlsx attached).
- Multi-division activation: we must be explicit in the PO payload which line item maps to which AWS account/email to avoid entitlement confusion. If Acme wants to designate two different buyer emails for the same PO, AWS sometimes objects; safer to have a single AWS buyer and map internal cost centers on your side.

I can turn around a short SOW addendum in ~24 hours once they confirm scope. If Acme insists on separate buyer activation per line item we should plan for two private offers to avoid implementation errors.

Jonas Weber
Marketplace Counsel | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Attachment: SOW-summary.xlsx (outline for Research pilot: usage caps, support window, data handling)

From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-06T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer question — splitting term/pricing across divisions

Thanks, everyone — that's super helpful. To confirm Acme's preferences:
- We'll use one canonical AWS buyer account: aws-purchases@acme-corp.com.
- We want a single private offer with two line items:
  - Line item A (CloudOps): 24 months, 5k seat-equivalent commit; preferred consolidated invoice.
  - Line item B (Research pilot): 12 months, 500 seat-equivalent; do NOT auto-renew — Research will re-evaluate before month 12.
- Billing contact: procurement-billing@acme-corp.com
- Legal: we'll accept Redwood's standard T&Cs and attach the SOW addendum for Research.

If you can send the DocuSign for commercial acceptance and the HubSpot record updated, we can route internally and return a signed PO within 48 business hours.

Lydia Park
Procurement Manager | Acme Corp
